duplicates.why: Both rest on one fact: NetworkPolicy ingress and egress are independent directions and both isolated ends must allow a connection. Knowing that ingress isolation leaves egress open (1.1-01, T) gives the answer that a destination ingress allowance cannot override source egress denial (1.1-03, F), and 1.1-03's explanation states it outright.

Same false template ('<controller> in warn mode rejects violations'); a player who learns one answers the other. 4.1-01 is the core CKS fact (Pod Security Admission), 5.2-08 is the repeat.

edits.notes:
I checked each rewrite against the official page text. I downloaded the raw page and searched it for the exact quote, not a summary. Web search was unavailable (budget used up), so all checks used direct page fetches. All statements are at most 120 characters, and all explanations at most 240.

Choices that go beyond the verifiers' suggestions:
(1) 2.2-02: I did not use the verifier's text "A kubelet in AlwaysAllow authorization mode denies ...". The mode name gives the answer away. I kept the same fact (AlwaysAllow is not RBAC) but describe the mode by its flag default, confirmed in the kubelet flag reference: --authorization-mode Default "AlwaysAllow". The statement names flags-only configuration, so the Webhook default of KubeletConfiguration does not apply.
(2) 6.2-01 is dropped. No allowed official page says that existing binaries still run under readOnlyRootFilesystem. Because of that drop, 6.2-02, 6.2-05 and 6.2-10 are all rewritten instead of dropped.
(3) 5.2-08 is dropped as the scan duplicate. It is also a name giveaway ("warn mode rejects"). As a result, both 5.2-01 and 5.2-03 are rewritten.
(4) 4.1: I rewrote 01 (unlabeled namespace defaults to Privileged) and dropped 06. This removes the psa-warn-mode and psa-controller-created-pods give-aways in one step.
(5) 1.3-08: I trimmed the explanation so it no longer states 5.2-05's identity-plus-OIDC-issuer fact.
(6) I lightly reworded several verifier statements to avoid words the scan identified as tells. Examples: 1.3-06 "proves" became "shows"; I avoided "none" in 3.2-02 and 3.2-07, "also" in 4.2-06, and "confines" in 3.2-05. In 1.2-04, 3.1-01, 5.3-03 and 6.1-04 I adjusted length only to keep each section within the 5-character rule.

Tell rewrites (5): 1.1-10, 1.2-03, 4.3-01, 5.2-06 and 6.1-04. They remove false-only proof and coverage words (confirms, establishes, confines, automatically) and move "confirms" into a true card. The deck-wide pattern the scan calls the "pessimist rule" (risk claims are true, protection claims are false) is semantic and remains. It needs new card choices, not rewording.

Templates still open:
- "Falco event proves more than it records" (6.2-07, 6.2-08, 6.2-09, 6.2-10) still has 4 false cards. 6.2-10 had to be rewritten, not dropped, and the verifier's replacement keeps the pattern. This should be fixed in a later pass.

For the orchestrator:

- Set volatility to may_change for: 2.2-09 (support window); 1.3-04 (spec.externalIPs is deprecated in v1.36 and its removal is planned); policy-controller cards 5.2-01, 5.2-02, 5.2-07 and 5.2-09 (component still under active development, CRD v1beta1).

cards.statement: A kubectl.sha256 match from dl.k8s.io gives the same assurance of the publisher's identity as cosign verify-blob.
cards.explanation: A checksum only shows the bytes match the published hash file; cosign verify-blob checks a signature and certificate tied to the Kubernetes release signing identity.
cards.reason: Wording lens fix adopted: removes the proof verb 'establishes', which the deck uses mostly on false cards. Fact unchanged; verify-signed-artifacts uses cosign verify-blob with certificate identity and OIDC issuer.

cards.statement: A ServiceAccount's automountServiceAccountToken: false blocks token mounts in Pods that set the field to true.
cards.explanation: When both set the field, the Pod spec takes precedence, so a Pod can re-enable the token mount; enforce the restriction with admission policy.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; Configure Service Accounts page: 'the Pod spec takes precedence.'

cards.statement: A kubelet configured by command-line flags alone, all at their defaults, checks each request against Kubernetes RBAC.
cards.explanation: The kubelet flag defaults to AlwaysAllow, which allows every request; RBAC applies only in Webhook mode, where the kubelet asks the API server through a SubjectAccessReview.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; kubelet reference: --authorization-mode Default "AlwaysAllow", Webhook mode uses SubjectAccessReview.

cards.statement: With anonymous access on, a kubelet using Webhook authentication treats credential-free requests as system:anonymous.
cards.explanation: Requests that no configured authenticator rejects fall through to the anonymous authenticator; only disabling anonymous access turns them into 401 responses.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; kubelet authn/authz page documents system:anonymous and --anonymous-auth=false giving 401.

cards.statement: Upstream Kubernetes patch releases, including security fixes, cover the three most recent minor versions.
cards.explanation: The project maintains release branches for the three newest minors, each with about a year of patch support; a cluster on an older minor stops receiving upstream security fixes.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; kubernetes.io/releases states branches for the most recent three minors and about 1 year of patch support. Volatility may_change.

cards.statement: kube-controller-manager can give each built-in controller its own ServiceAccount and system:controller role.
cards.explanation: With --use-service-account-credentials each controller gets its own identity and role; without it, every control loop shares the controller manager's single credential.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; RBAC page Controller roles section confirms per-controller service accounts and system:controller: roles.

cards.statement: An admission rule blocking a runtime socket's exact path can leave access through a parent hostPath mount.
cards.explanation: A hostPath mount of a directory above the socket still exposes the socket, so policy has to forbid mounts that include it directly or through a parent directory.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; API server bypass risks page: restrict hostPath mounts that include the runtime socket 'either directly or by mounting a parent directory'.

cards.statement: On a node where the kubelet tolerates swap, missing tmpfs noswap support makes the kubelet refuse to start.
cards.explanation: The kubelet logs a warning that memory-backed volumes such as Secrets might swap to disk, then keeps running; provisioning encrypted swap is the administrator's job.
cards.reason: Fact lens fix adopted: on a 'swap-enabled node' the kubelet does refuse to start by default (failSwapOn true), so the old wording was defensibly True. Confirmed on the v1.35 swap page: 'If the noswap option is not supported, kubelet will emit a warning log entry, then continue its execution'; encrypted swap is outside the kubelet's scope.

cards.statement: A process under an AppArmor profile in complain mode completes a file write outside the profile's rules.
cards.explanation: Complain mode only reports profile violations and does not block them, so it suits profile development rather than containment; switch to enforce mode before relying on it.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; linux-kernel-security-constraints: complain mode 'only reports violations'.

cards.statement: A node's /sys/kernel/security/apparmor/profiles file names the container processes attached to each listed profile.
cards.explanation: That file lists loaded profiles and their modes. To see the profile a container's root process runs under, read /proc/1/attr/current inside the container.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; AppArmor tutorial uses the profiles file for loaded profiles and /proc/1/attr/current for the container.

cards.statement: With externalTrafficPolicy Cluster, kube-proxy on a node hosting zero of a Service's Pods forwards its NodePort traffic.
cards.explanation: Each node proxies a NodePort Service's port, so every node becomes an entry point; restrict exposure with node firewalls or kube-proxy nodePortAddresses.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; Service page: 'Each node proxies that port' and nodePortAddresses configuration.

cards.statement: Moving a RuntimeDefault seccomp Pod from containerd nodes to CRI-O nodes can change its allowed syscall set.
cards.explanation: RuntimeDefault defers to each node runtime's bundled profile, and runtimes and their releases can ship different syscall lists, so test the workload on every runtime it may run on.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; seccomp tutorial says default profiles can differ between CRI-O and containerd and their releases.

cards.statement: Pod Security Admission enforces Baseline in an unlabeled namespace when its AdmissionConfiguration sets no defaults.
cards.explanation: With no namespace labels and no configured defaults, Pod Security Admission applies the Privileged level, so it restricts nothing. Set labels or configuration defaults to enforce a level.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; PodSecurityConfiguration defaults show enforce: "privileged" as default.

cards.statement: With several etcd members, TLS on the API server's etcd client connection covers member-to-member replication traffic.
cards.explanation: etcd secures peer traffic with its own peer certificate and key, configured separately from client TLS; without it, data replicated between members travels unprotected.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; Operating etcd clusters documents separate --peer-key-file/--peer-cert-file for member communication.

cards.statement: With KMS v2, revoking the API server's access to the remote KEK immediately blocks reads that use already cached DEKs.
cards.explanation: KMS v2 caches unwrapped DEKs in the clear and keeps decrypting with them indefinitely without calling the KMS, so revoking KEK access does not block reads that use those cached keys.
cards.reason: Wording lens fix adopted: 'at once' parsed two ways. Fact unchanged and confirmed on kms-provider: cached DEKs 'can be used to perform decryption indefinitely without making a call to the KMS'.

cards.statement: An attacker who compromises a control plane host can extract a locally managed aescbc key that protects Secrets in etcd.
cards.explanation: The local key is stored on the host in the EncryptionConfiguration file, so local encryption protects against an etcd-only compromise but not against a host compromise.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; encrypt-data page states local keys protect against etcd compromise but not host compromise.

cards.statement: On one node, two RuntimeClasses with different names give their Pods the same isolation when they share a handler.
cards.explanation: A RuntimeClass's handler names the CRI configuration on the node and its object name only identifies the RuntimeClass, so a sandbox-sounding name adds no isolation when the handler points at an ordinary runtime.
cards.reason: Wording lens fix adopted ('X, rather than Y, determines' marked True), with 'On one node' added because RuntimeClass scheduling allows heterogeneous nodes where one handler name could map to different configurations. Runtime Class page: the handler name 'identifies the configuration' and homogeneous nodes are assumed by default.

cards.statement: With ordinary containers sharing a worker node, namespace separation keeps a container escape inside its tenant.
cards.explanation: Namespaces group API resources and policies; they do not separate a shared node's kernel.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; Multi-tenancy page: containers share a kernel and sandboxing is needed to insulate the host from container escapes.

cards.statement: A validly signed attestation passes cosign verify-attestation even when its predicate fails the supplied CUE policy.
cards.explanation: With --policy, cosign checks the attestation's predicate against CUE or Rego rules and reports validation errors on any violation, even when the signature itself is valid.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; Sigstore attestation page shows --policy with CUE/Rego and a validation-error output on failure.

cards.statement: By default, a Trivy CycloneDX image report is a package inventory that omits vulnerability findings.
cards.explanation: Trivy treats CycloneDX output as an SBOM: --format cyclonedx turns off security scanning by default, and vulnerabilities appear only with --scanners vuln.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; Trivy SBOM page: '--format cyclonedx disables security scanning'.

cards.statement: By default, policy-controller rejects an image in an opted-in namespace when no ClusterImagePolicy pattern matches it.
cards.explanation: Without a no-match-policy setting, policy-controller denies images that match no ClusterImagePolicy, so unlisted registries stay blocked; warn or allow relaxes this.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; policy-controller overview: unmatched images are rejected when no-match-policy is not configured.

cards.statement: A ValidatingAdmissionPolicy CEL rule can reject Deployments whose container images use an unapproved registry prefix.
cards.explanation: The v1.35 docs show a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that checks container image prefixes with CEL, so the API server enforces permitted registries without a webhook.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; v1.35 VAP page has the image startsWith example on Deployments.

cards.statement: Cosign verification confirms the signed digest matches the target image while default claim checks stay on.
cards.explanation: Cosign's claim checks compare the image digest in the signature payload with the image being verified.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; Sigstore verify page: cosign validates by default that the payload digest matches the container.

cards.statement: An ignore-check annotation in a workload's own manifest can make KubeLinter skip that check for the object.
cards.explanation: KubeLinter honors ignore-check.kube-linter.io/<check> and kube-linter.io/ignore-all annotations, so a clean result can reflect an author's exemption rather than a compliant setting.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; configuring-kubelinter.md documents both annotations.

cards.statement: By default, a Trivy image scan also reports secrets found in image files alongside vulnerable packages.
cards.explanation: Trivy enables vulnerability and secret scanning by default for container images, so credentials left in image files appear in results; misconfiguration and license scanning stay off unless enabled.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; Trivy container image page: 'By default, vulnerability and secret scanning are enabled'.

cards.statement: Putting container.id in a Falco rule's output restricts that rule's matches to events from container processes.
cards.explanation: Falco's condition selects event scope. Printing container.id adds context to an alert rather than filtering host events.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; Falco basic rule elements: the condition filters events, the output only formats the alert.

cards.statement: Falco rule outputs can name a container shell's grandparent and earlier ancestor processes alongside its parent.
cards.explanation: Ancestor fields such as proc.aname[2] and proc.apid[2] take an index, so an alert can show the chain from a shell back to the process that started the session.
cards.reason: Wording lens fix adopted to avoid field-name trivia (proc.apid's 'a' hints ancestor). Confirmed on Falco supported fields: proc.aname[1] is the parent, proc.aname[2] the grandparent, same indexing for proc.apid.

cards.statement: Falco's incubating Change thread namespace rule excludes setns calls made by runc during container setup.
cards.explanation: setns often runs while a container is created, so the rule's condition excludes runc, containerd and other known tools; it alerts on setns by an unexpected program, such as an nsenter escape attempt.
cards.reason: Both lenses found the rewrite wrong: the condition contains 'not proc.name startswith "runc"' and 'not proc.cmdline startswith "containerd"' (confirmed on falco.org default rules and falco-incubating_rules.yaml). Took the fact lens's True form over the wording lens's False flip because section 6.2, after 6.2-01's drop, would otherwise fall to 3 true versus 6 false; with this card it is 4 true, 5 false.

cards.statement: Falco's upper-layer executable flag also marks a binary that an attacker drops into a mounted emptyDir volume.
cards.explanation: proc.is_exe_upper_layer reports executables in the overlayfs upper layer. An emptyDir is node storage mounted into the Pod, so binaries dropped there fall outside that flag.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; supported-fields defines proc.is_exe_upper_layer as overlayfs upper layer; emptyDir is node-backed storage. 'X covers emptyDir' false template is at its limit of two (6.2-04, 6.2-10).

cards.statement: When a policy and its matching rule both list omitStages, kube-apiserver omits the union of the two lists.
cards.explanation: Policy-wide and rule-level omitStages combine, so a rule cannot re-enable a stage that the policy omits; stages in neither list still produce events.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep; audit v1 reference: 'the union of both are omitted'.
